papers.title: Translation of in vivo CAR-T in China
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 22 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00509-4 China’s rapid progress in in vivo chimeric antigen receptor (CAR)-T cell therapy reflects strengths of its biotechnology sector, which brings together research institutions, industry and hospitals to advance this emerging treatment. Drawing on our experience, we discuss how this expansion occurred and how speed and scale can be converted into original, clinically differentiated therapies.

papers.title: What closed-loop insulin delivery can — and cannot — teach us
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 09 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00497-5 Closed-loop insulin delivery is one of the great success stories of autonomous medicine. Its legacy, however, is not a universal blueprint, but the recognition that each closed-loop system must be designed around the biology, risks and lived realities of each condition.

papers.title: Anticipatory intelligence in clinical microbiology
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 08 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00502-x Clinical microbiology needs an artificial intelligence system that predicts pathogen evolution and resistance to enable prevention. Laboratories should connect forecasts to confirmatory experiments and defined actions, then test them prospectively across time and populations, as well as govern false alarms, model updates and inequitable performance as carefully as diagnostic errors.

papers.title: Fibre-architected intelligent permeable bioelectronics
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 06 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00500-z Fibre-architected intelligent permeable bioelectronics (FIPEB) use soft, porous and multiscale fibre networks to overcome the rigidity and impermeability of conventional bioelectronics, enabling stable interfaces with dynamic biological tissues. This Review highlights how FIPEB materials, properties and scalable fabrication strategies can advance digital health care through continuous monitoring, personalized diagnosis and closed-loop therapeutic systems.

papers.title: What it takes to commercialize a bone graft
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00503-w Commercializing a bio-hybrid synthetic and xenogeneic bone graft requires integrated design that treats clinical and translational constraints as product requirements. Drawing on established components and validated concepts, we developed SmartBone as an effective composite solution. Here, we share key lessons from its commercialization, including systems engineering and the need for long-term performance evidence.

papers.title: Plant immune receptor engineering
papers.summary: Nature Reviews Bioengineering, Published online: 05 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s44222-026-00499-3 This Review highlights advances for identifying, transferring and engineering plant immune receptors, then discusses translational strategies for developing durable, sustainable crop protection.

pipeline.content: [PHASE1] RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases (NIAID) | 适应症: HIV. This Phase 1 study will evaluate the safety, tolerability, and immune responses of investigational CH505 HIV vaccine regimens in adults in overall good health without HIV. Participants will receive CH505 protein nanoparticle vaccines (DV901-NP) formulated with the investigational adjuvant ACU-026-001-1, followed by either CH505 protein nanoparticle (DV902-NP) or CH505 mRNA vaccine boosters. The study will assess the ability of these regimens to induce HIV-specific immune responses, including B-cell responses associated with the development of broadly neutralizing antibodies. An immunology cohort will also evaluate how the location of booster vaccination affects immune responses.

pipeline.title: Integrated Mindfulness-based Health Qigong Intervention for COVID-19 Survivors and Caregivers
pipeline.content: [NA] COMPLETED | 申办方/赞助方: TSANG Hector Wing-Hong | 适应症: COVID-19 Infection. This study examines the effectiveness of a 16-week Integrated Mindfulness-based Health Qigong (iMBHQ) program, delivered via a mobile application, in improving the mental and physical well-being of COVID-19 survivors, their caregivers, and the general public. We hypothesize that participants in the iMBHQ group will demonstrate significant reductions in stress, depression, and anxiety compared to a control group receiving treatment-as-usual. This parallel-group randomized controlled trial aims to recruit 600 participants (200 COVID-19 survivors, 200 caregivers, and 200 individuals from the general public). Effectiveness is evaluated at baseline, 8 weeks, 16 weeks, 6 months, 12 months and 18 months post-intervention, using standardized psychological and physical health assessments.

pipeline.title: Pandemic Influenza Vaccine in Organ Transplantation (PIVOT Trial)
pipeline.content: [PHASE3] ACTIVE_NOT_RECRUITING | 申办方/赞助方: University Health Network, Toronto | 适应症: Influenza (Pandemic), Avian Influenza, Vaccination. Influenza is an important pathogen in transplant recipients. The current widespread outbreak of highly pathogenic H5N1 avian influenza (HPAI) in livestock, and the occurrence of several human cases of infection suggest that the next influenza pandemic may be soon approaching. Transplant patients will likely be uniquely predisposed to serious infection with high morbidity and mortality. There are a number of important reasons that evaluation of prevention strategies are critical in this highly vulnerable population. Currently, there is no data on the immunogenicity of H5Nx vaccines in this highly vulnerable population. The investigators plan to study the safety and immunogenicity of a two-dose regimen of the pandemic influenza H5N1 vaccine in organ transplant patients.

There are many different types of Streptococcus pneumoniae bacteria, called serotypes. Vaccines contain small parts of certain serotypes. This phase I trial studies the side effects and best dose of vaccine therapy when given together with sargramostim in treating patients with locally advanced or metastatic pancreatic cancer that cannot be removed by surgery. This phase II clinical trial tests how well the cytomegalovirus-modified vaccinica Ankara (CMV-MVA) Triplex vaccine given to human leukocyte antigens (HLA) matched related stem cell donors works to prevent cytomegalovirus (CMV) infection in patients undergoing hematopoietic stem cell transplant. The CMV-MVA Triplex vaccine works by causing an immune response in the donors body to the CMV virus, creating immunity to it. The donor then passes that immunity on to the patient upon receiving the stem cell transplant. Giving the CMV-MVA triplex vaccine to donors may help prevent CMV infection of patients undergoing stem cell transplantation.

Vaccines made from the survivin peptide or antigen may help the body build an effective immune response to kill tumor cells that express survivin.
